title: Sponsor and readiness pressure test
objective: Decide go, narrow or reschedule when the worksheet is empty and sponsorship is unconfirmed.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Before Visioning, test whether the session can succeed. A workshop without the basics wastes the customer's goodwill and produces a use case list nobody owns.

items: Sponsor alignment, or a credible and documented path to it.
The relevant stakeholders invited, with the right lines of business represented.
A clear outcome for the session, an agenda, and working facilitation tools.

blocks.x: Glean's Visioning playbook is direct: decline or reschedule if pre-work, survey responses, or executive sponsor alignment are missing.

items: "Who owns the KPI we would move?"
"Who can sponsor the next investment decision?"

blocks.x: If the answers are vague, schedule a narrower alignment conversation before the full workshop.

items: **Narrow:** some basics are missing but the meeting is valuable. Convert it into a qualification and alignment conversation, and say so.
**Reschedule:** pre-work is empty and the sponsor path is unknown.

blocks.label: Note on sponsor attendance
blocks.x: Glean sources differ on whether the executive sponsor should attend early Visioning. Champion-led Visioning can work, but Executive Validation must still resolve executive alignment. Don't turn a preferred attendance pattern into a universal rule.
The readiness review ends in one of three decisions. Make the call explicitly, and tell the champion why.

blocks.title: Go, narrow, or reschedule
blocks.alt: A comparison of the three readiness decisions with when each applies: go when the sponsor, priorities, and attendees are confirmed; narrow when only part of the scope is ready; reschedule when the decision-makers or business owners can't attend.

items.b: Sponsor, priorities, and the right attendees are confirmed
Only one team or use case area is ready
Decision-makers or business owners can't attend
